newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Rally extended despite softer U.S..
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Rally extended despite softer U.S..

text.p: Weekly Asian MTBE prices extended their rally by another $5.00 per tonne amid tight supplies despite the softer U.S. market, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Singapore free-on-board (fob) supplies in September have already traded at $285 per tonne this week, the level at which the few remaining supplies are offered, traders said.
Cargoes traded last week at $280, extending the rally since June, mainly on the back of strong U.S prices.

But U.S. prices have softened amid shortcovering at lower prices. But the tone for September is firmer as concerns that mid-August supplies would improve were overshadowed by talk of an unplanned shutdown of a 16,000 barrel-per-day Saudi Basic Inductries Corp (SABIC) and Shell joint-venture plant.
"The Singapore quote is firm not so much because of the U.S. but because the product is tight...most of Singapore parcels are already committed," a producer said.
But one seller of a large 10,000 to 15,000 tonne cargo of September MTBE preferred to sell on a U.S. linked formula.
"There are one or two enquiries for regional use, but the U.S. is still more competitive," the seller said.
The arbitrage window to the U.S. West Coast was still wide open with Singapore about $30-$40 per tonne lower.
"Eventhough the U.S. number is declining, as long as there is a difference of $20, traders can still make it (the arbitrage)," a trader said.
Reflecting the firmer market, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) last week paid $20 more for its September requirements than for August.
CPC purchased two 3,500-tonne cargoes from two companies at around $290 per tonne, cost-and-freight Kaohsiung or Keelung, a company official said.
